sentences.text: This petition is filed by the petitioner against respondents for seeking compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

02. The brief facts of case of the petitioner is that:
(SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.361/2020 On 08-01-2020 at about 08.30 a.m, the petitioner was riding his Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-05-EK-560 on the left side of Chamarajapete 7th Cross, at Mysore Road, at that time the rider of Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-36-EH-5588 proceeding from same direction, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's Motor Cycle from behind.

Due to which petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries and immediately after the accident he was shifted to the Venlakh hospital, Bengaluru, wherein admitted as inpatient from 08.01.2020 to 11.01.2020 and has undergone surgery and has spent Rs.3,00,000/- towards treatment.

Due to accidental injuries, he is unable to do his routine work and sustained great loss and prior to accident he was hale and healthy and was aged about 56 years and was working as Account Consultant and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.

The accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the aforesaid offending Motor Cycle by its rider and in this regard the Chickpet Traffic Police have registered a case against the said offending Motor Cycle rider.

Hence, the respondent No.1 being the R.C. owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurer of the said offending Motor Cycle, are jointly and severally liable (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.361/2020 to pay compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% p.a and costs.
03. On service of notice, the respondent No.2 has appeared before the tribunal through its counsel and filed written statement.
Inspite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 remained absent and hence, he was placed exparte.

04. Respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied the entire case of the petitioner and further denied alleged accident, negligence of the rider of offending Motor Cycle, age, avocation, income of the petitioner and nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and treatment taken by the petitioner and expenses incurred by the petitioner and admits that this respondent has issued a Two-wheeler Package Policy bearing No:OG-20-1701-1802-00024049 in favour fo respondent No.1 in respect of Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-36-EH-5588 and it is valid from 24.08.2019 to 23.08.2020 and the liability if any is subject to terms conditions of the policy.

The petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties and the earlier Police records reveal that the Motor Cycle bearing T.R. Vinayaka vs Veeresh Patil on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56067937/
2 No.KA-16-EH-8866 which caused the accident.

Under these circumstances the petitioner has not filed a false case as against the insured vehicle and the (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.361/2020 respondent No.1 had been willfully entrusted his vehicle to a person who did not possess valid and effective driving licence to ride the same as on the date of accident and hence, there is violation of terms and conditions of the policy.
The compensation claimed is highly excessive, exorbitant and pray for dismiss the petition against respondent No.2 with costs.

05. On the basis of the above pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor has framed the following Issues:-
ISSUES 01.

Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 08.01.2020 at about 08.30 a.m, at Mysore Road, 9th Cross Junction, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent act of the riding of the Motor Cycle bearing registration No. KA-36-EH-5588 by its rider as alleged in the petition?
02. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
03. What Order or Award?
06.

The petitioner in order to prove his case, he himself examined as PW.1 and got examined doctor who examined the petitioner and assessed the (SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.361/2020 disability as PW.2 and through them got marked 20 documents as Ex.P.1 to 20 and closed the petitioner side evidence.
The Senior Executive of the respondent No.2 Insurance Company got examined as RW.1 and got marked 4 documents as Ex.R.1 to 4 and closed its side evidence.
07. I have heard the arguments advanced by the learned counsels for the petitioner and the respondent No.2 and perused the records.

08. My findings on the above Issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 In the Negative  Issue No.2 In the Negative  Issue No.3

As per final order  for the following:-
 REASONS 09. Issue No.1:- The petitioner in order to prove his case, he himself examined as PW.1 and in his chief-examination evidence he has reiterated the petition averments therein.

During the course of T.R. Vinayaka vs Veeresh Patil on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56067937/
3 cross-examination by the respondent No.2 counsel, he admits that he came to know that there are different vehicle number in Complaint, FIR and in Charge sheet (SCCH-3) 7 M.V.C.No.361/2020 and he has not intimated by writing to the Police to rectify the vehicle number and he has lodged complaint.

sentences.text: Later he gave further statement as the vehicle number was wrongly mentioned and also stated that when he was riding Motor Cycle due to repair of road he stop his vehicle and that time the offending Motor Cycle came and dashed from behind.

But offending Motor Cycle has not sustained any damages and he note down the offending Motor Cycle number at the accident spot itself and based upon the vehicle number noted down at the accident spot, he lodged the complaint to the Police and based upon his complaint, case was registered and offending Motor Cycle has not sustained damages and also admits that the vehicle number mentioned in his complaint has caused accident to him and he has not produced any further statement and he do not remember when his further statement was recorded and also admits that in his complaint he has mentioned that the vehicle bearing No.KA-36-EH-8866 has caused accident.
He came to know that the vehicle bearing No. KA-36-EH-5588 has caused the accident after 4-5 months and admits that even now he has intimated to the Police about the difference in vehicle number.

The Police have not recorded his further statement and (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.361/2020 also admits that after lodging complaint the Police have not called him for any procedure of investigation and he cannot say the color and company of vehicle which caused accident to him.
He came to know about the offending vehicle number through the hospital authority and the hospital authority were not present at the accident spot.
He was taken to hospital by the offending rider of Motor Cycle.
He did not inform the manner of accident in the hospital, but the said rider of Motor Cycle had only informed.

The said offending Motor Cycle rider had only informed the vehicle number and denied to the suggestion that vehicle bearing No.KA-36-EH-8866 had caused accident to him and as there was no document the vehicle bearing No.KA-36-EH-5588 was falsely implicated in this case to claim the compensation and also denied to the suggestion that vehicle bearing No.KA-36-EH-5588 had not caused accident and denied to the suggestion that in collusion with Police and respondent No.1, false case is registered against the offending rider of the Motor Cycle.
10.

During the course of cross-examination once he stated that he note down the offending Motor Cycle number at the accident spot itself and based upon the vehicle number noted down at the accident (SCCH-3) 9 M.V.C.No.361/2020 spot, he lodged the complaint to the Police.
Based upon his complaint, case was registered and offending Motor Cycle has not sustained damages.

Further,
he stated that he came to know about the offending vehicle number through the hospital authority and also admits that in his complaint he has mentioned that the vehicle bearing No.KA-36-EH-8866 has caused accident and he came to know that the vehicle bearing No.KA-36-EH-5588 has caused the accident after 4-5 months.

Though he stated once Police have recorded further statement regarding vehicle number, but later changed his version stating that the Police have not recorded his further statement and also admits that after lodging complaint the Police have not called him for any procedure of investigation and he cannot say the color and company of vehicle which caused accident to him and he was taken to hospital by the offending rider of Motor Cycle.
But in this regard there is no mentioning in the medical records produced by the petitioner.

11. Further, PW.2 is a Doctor, who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability of the petitioner, has stated that the petitioner sustained communited bicondylar fracture of left leg near T.R. Vinayaka vs Veeresh Patil on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56067937/
4 knee proximal tibia bone with intra articular extension and (SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.361/2020 he assessed disability of left lower limb at 38.6% and whole body disability at 12.86% and he has produced IP record, Police intimation, Disability assessment report with calculation, X-rays and MRI film as per Ex.P.16 to 20.

During the course of cross-examination by the respondent No.2 counsel he stated that Dr.Prashanth.J, Orthopedic surgeon in their hospital has treated the petitioner and has given surgical treatment and before assessing disability, he has not taken written opinion from the Orthopedic Surgeon and he was general physician and he has assist the Orthopedic Surgeon while conducting surgery and he was part of the team of the doctors who treated the petitioner.
There is no other complications at fractures site.
There was a restrictions of movement.
There is no bone loss.
There is no limb shortening.
There is no loss of muscle power.
Implants are already removed.
Range of movement in hip and ankle is normal.
Range of movements can be improved by physiotherapy.
Range of movements improved then existing disability can come down.
Orthopedic surgeon has not given disability certificate.
12. Apart from the oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked 20 documents as Ex.P.1 to 20 on his behalf.

Ex.P.1 is copy of FIR filed by the Chickpet (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.361/2020 Traffic Police against the rider of the offending Motor Cycle, wherein the offending Motor Cycle number is mentioned as KA-36-EH-8866.

Ex.P.2 is copy of Complaint lodged by the petitioner himself,
wherein also he mentioned the registration number of the offending Motor Cycle as KA-36-EH-8866 which was allegedly caused accident.

Ex.P.3 is copy of Spot Mahazar, wherein it is stated that one eye-witness Suresh has shown the accident spot stating that the Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-36-EH-5588 has caused the accident and in his presence the Police have conducted Mahazar.

Ex.P.4 is copy of IMV report of the vehicle number KA-05-EK-560 of the petitioner,
wherein front wheel mudguard damaged and left crash guard damaged.
Ex.P.5 is copy of IMV report of the offending vehicle number KA-36-EH-5588.
But on perusal of the said document, it is found that there is no damages caused to the said vehicle.

In case, if really said Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-36-EH-5588 has caused accident, certainly the said Motor Cycle may also sustained damage and rider of the said Motor Cycle has also sustained injuries.
But neither the Motor Cycle was damaged nor rider of offending Motor Cycle was got injured.
It creates doubt regarding involvement of offending vehicle in the accident, which (SCCH-3) 12 M.V.C.No.361/2020 was allegedly caused accident.
Ex.P.6 is copy of Charge Sheet which discloses that the Investigation Officer after investigation has submitted Charge sheet against rider of offending Motor Cycle.
According to the Charge sheet, the rider of the offending Motor Cycle was after causing accident left the spot without providing treatment to the injured person.
But during the course of cross-examination, the PW.1 has stated that the rider of offending Motor Cycle himself was admitted him to hospital.
Therefore, there are two different and divergent version of the petitioner and the Charge sheet creates doubt regarding involvement of the offending Motor Cycle.
Ex.P.7 is copy of Wound certificate which shows the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident.
But in the said Wound certificate no vehicle number was mentioned which was caused accident.

Ex.P.8 is Discharge summary issued by Venlakh hospital, Bengaluru, wherein the petitioner was admitted as inpatient from 08.01.2020 and discharged on 11.01.2020 for 04 days due to accidental injuries.
Ex.P.12 is copy of Order sheet in CC 2772/2020, wherein the rider of the offending Motor Cycle was pleaded guilty and was convicted.

Ex.P.13 is copy of Plea recorded in the said case which also shows that (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.361/2020 the rider fo the said offending Motor Cycle was voluntarily T.R. Vinayaka vs Veeresh Patil on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56067937/
5 pleaded guilty.
Ex.P.14 is copy of Notice U/Sec.133 of IMV Act issued to the owner of the offending Motor Cycle.
Ex.P.15 is copy of Reply to notice, wherein the owner/respondent No.1 admits he is the owner of the offending Motor Cycle and he himself caused the accident.
Ex.P.16 is IP record.
Even on perusal of Ex.P.17 Police intimation.
Ex.P.18 is Disability assessment report with calculation.
Ex.P.19 is X-rays and Ex.P.20 is MRI film.
13. On behalf of the respondent No.2, its Senior Executive is examined as RW.1 and in her chief- examination evidence she has reiterated the written statement averments therein.

During the course of cross-examination by the petitioner counsel she stated that she deposed before the court on the basis of Police records and also admits that they have issued policy in favour of vehicle bearing No.KA-36-EH-5588 and said policy was valid as on the date of accident and also stated that except FIR, in Seizer Mahazar and other documents vehicle number was correctly mentioned, but she volunteers that insured vehicle was falsely implicated in the case and denied to the suggestion that in FIR the vehicle number KA-36-EH-8866 is mentioned due to typographical error and also stated (SCCH-3) 14 M.V.C.No.361/2020 that as per IMV report there is no visible damages to the offending vehicle and also stated that she does not know whether respondent No.1 has challenged the Charge sheet.
14.
On perusal of her evidence, it is suggested in the cross-examination to the RW.1 that due to typographical error vehicle number was wrongly mentioned as KA-36-EH-8866 in FIR.
But on perusal of Ex.P.2 Complaint itself vehicle number was mentioned as KA-36-EH-8866 and only in Spot Mahazar the vehicle number is mentioned as KA-36-EH-5588.
Moreover, as per Ex.P.5 IMV report no visible damage was found on the offending vehicle allegedly involved in the accident.

In case, if as contended by the petitioner in his pleadings and evidence that the rider of the offending Motor Cycle has rashly and negligently riding his Motor Cycle and dashed against the petitioners'
Motor Cycle from behind, if so, certainly the front portion of the offending Motor Cycle would have damaged.
But no such damages was found on the offending Motor Cycle.
It creates doubt regarding involvement of offending Motor Cycle in the accident.

Further, as already discussed earlier, the petitioner in his cross-examination has stated that he has note down (SCCH-3) 15 M.V.C.No.361/2020 the offending Motor Cycle number at the accident spot itself and he has lodged the complaint to the Police and also stated that he came to know that there are different vehicle number in Complaint, FIR and in Charge sheet, but he has not intimated by writing to the Police to rectify the vehicle number and also admits that in his complaint he has mentioned that the vehicle bearing No.KA-36-EH-8866 has caused accident and he came to know that the vehicle bearing No.KA-36-EH-5588 has caused the accident after 4-5 months and Police have not recorded his further statement to rectify the vehicle number.

Once he stated that he himself take down the vehicle number at the accident spot and again in the cross-examination he stated that he came to know about the offending vehicle number through the hospital authority.
Therefore, it creates doubt regarding involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident.
15. The petitioner counsel has argued that the rider of the offending Motor Cycle has himself pleaded guilty and paid penalty as per Ex.P.12 and 13.
But eventhough the owner of the offending vehicle in unmistakable terms has admitted the accident, that admission has no value in the eye of law.

In this (SCCH-3) 16 M.V.C.No.361/2020 regard, the respondent No.2 counsel had relied upon T.R. Vinayaka vs Veeresh Patil on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56067937/
6

sentences.text:
the following Judgments:-
01. ILR 2009 KAR 3562 (DB) in a case of Veerappa and another V/s Siddappa and another, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has held that, "(A) Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 - Accident claim - Dismissal of claim petition - Appealed against "FRAUS ET JUS MUNQUAM COHABITANT " -
Fraud and Justice Never Dwell Together - An attempt on the part of the 1st respondent/Owner to collude with the claimants with the fond hope of saddling the Insurance Company to pay compensation - 1st respondent/Owner of the vehicle admitted the accident and had no objection for award of compensation -

entities.text: Veerappa and another V/s Siddappa and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Held, Even though the owner of the vehicle in unmistakable terms, has admitted the accident, that admission has no value in the eye of law.
He has admitted something about which he has no knowledge and, which he has not seen.
It is clear that the said admission is made with the sole object of getting compensation to the claimants as it is the Insurance Company which will pay, and not the owner.
Though admission is the best piece of evidence, it cannot be accepted as gospel truth.
The Court can insist on proof of facts, if the admission is not (SCCH-3) 17 M.V.C.No.361/2020 satisfactory.
In the instant case, since the Court was not satisfied, it wanted the claimants to prove their case independently.
The claimants have miserably failed to prove their case.

"(B) Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 - Accident - Claim petition - Dismissal of - Fraud played on the Courts by the claimants with the connivance of the 1st respondent - Liability of the Insurance Company to pay the compensation if the fraud is proved - Held, Insurance Company not liable to indemnify the owner of the vehicle who has played fraud and not liable to pay any compensation to the claimants who are also party to the fraud - Further Held, It is a clear case of fraud played on the Court by the claimants with the connivance of 1st respondent.

Once the insured plays fraud,
admits liability with the sole object of foisting liability on the Insurance Company,
though in fact he knew that it is not true, liability of the Insurance Company to indemnify such insured ceases.

Therefore, there is no obligation on the part of the Insurance Company to indemnify the insured even though he has taken the policy and the statute mandates that the Insurance Company has to indemnify the insured and pay compensation to third party.
When fraud is established from the material on record, such (SCCH-3) 18 M.V.C.No.361/2020 statutory obligation stands discharged.
- There is no third party liability on the part of the Insurance Company to pay compensation to the claimants.
This amount is awarded in order to see that in future such false defences are not filed before Court, judicial process is not abused.
Therefore, it is only the 1st respondent/Owner who is liable to pay the amount.

Dismissal of Claim Petition against the Insurance Company is affirmed".
02. ILR 2009 KAR 2921 in a case of Bajaj Allianz Insurance Company Limited V/s B.C.Kumar and another, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has held that, Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 - Accident claim - Award - Insurance Company Appeal - Plea of Guilt by the driver - Conviction in the criminal case - Can the plea of guilt by the driver become the sole criterion for allowing the claim T.R. Vinayaka vs Veeresh Patil on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56067937/

entities.text: Bajaj Allianz Insurance Company Limited V/s B.C.Kumar and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7 petition by the MACT - A case of Insurance Company disputing the very factum of accident - Sustainability of the award passed by the MACT - Held, The MACT should not and ought not to place sole reliance on the Judgment of the Criminal Court while considering the issue of the factum of the accident and the consequent negligence, as stated in the claim petition filed before the tribunal.
But, the (SCCH-3) 19 M.V.C.No.361/2020 tribunal will have to assess the evidence before it independently of any finding of the Criminal Court on the question of the driver pleading guilty.
At the most, the circumstance of the driver pleading guilty may be considered as one of the pieces of evidence to support the case of the claimant.

But, the tribunal should not place implicit reliance only on the circumstance of the driver having pleaded guilty before the Criminal Court and such an approach by the tribunals will be not only an one sided approach but, at the same time, there is every likelihood of the pleading of guilt by a driver before the Criminal Court having been obtained by adopting various methods so as to ensure that the claimant succeeds before the MACT in getting compensation.
- Further Held, There has been spate of cases wherein false claims have been made before the claims tribunal and false implications are also on the increase.

The MACTs are constituted not only to allow the claim petitions which are genuine in nature but, at the same time,
the tribunals also will have to keep in view that compensation should not be awarded mechanically in every case and to accept the case of the claimant as if all that the claimant says about the accident and the injuries is a truthful one.

Merely because a claimant in a particular case comes out with (SCCH-3) 20 M.V.C.No.361/2020 the evidence that the driver of the vehicle is convicted on his pleading guilty, the tribunal should not go by the plead guilty factor alone, but it is required to appreciate the evidence before it from every angle and if there is a good reason to question the very case of the claimant or doubt the very manner of the accident, in such cases, the tribunal will have to view the factor of pleading guilty along with the entire evidence placed before it and made an assessment of the whole situation.
- Award passed by the tribunal is not justified.

Appeal is allowed".
16.
I have gone through the above said citations relied upon by the respondent No.2 Insurance Company.
The citations relied upon by the respondent No.2 Insurance Company amply applicable to the facts and circumstance of the case on hand.

On going through the entire evidence, it appears that offending insured vehicle was falsely implicated in the case with connivance of petitioner,
respondent No.1 and Police in order to get the compensation from the Insurance Company.
Because eventhough as per Spot Mahazar one eye-witness who is cited as CW.2 in the Charge sheet has stated vehicle number and witnessed the accident.

But petitioner has not examined the said eye- witness and even not examined the Investigation (SCCH-3) 21 M.V.C.No.361/2020 Officer to prove the fact that the insured vehicle was actually involved in the accident and no other vehicle was involved in the accident and even no visible damages was found to the insured vehicle as it is alleged that the said offending vehicle has dashed against behind the Motor Cycle of the petitioner, certainly offending vehicle should have damaged and no such damage was found and even petitioner has not produced MLC to proof of involvement of insured vehicle.
Therefore, the petitioner has failed to prove the involvement of the insured vehicle in the accident and rash and negligent riding of the rider of the insured vehicle.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the Negative.
17. Issue No.2:-

As discussed above, the petitioner has miserably failed to prove the involvement of insured vehicle in the accident and rash and negligent riding by its rider, certainly the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation from the hands of this tribunal.

Accordingly, I answered Issue T.R. Vinayaka vs Veeresh Patil on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56067937/
8 No.2 in the Negative.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Once he stated that he himself take down the vehicle number at the accident spot and again in the cross-examination he stated that he came to know about the offending vehicle number through the hospital authority.
Therefore, it creates doubt regarding involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident.
But eventhough the owner of the offending vehicle in unmistakable terms has admitted the accident, that admission has no value in the eye of law.
Held, Even though the owner of the vehicle in unmistakable terms, has admitted the accident, that admission has no value in the eye of law.
It is clear that the said admission is made with the sole object of getting compensation to the claimants as it is the Insurance Company which will pay, and not the owner.
Though admission is the best piece of evidence, it cannot be accepted as gospel truth.
The Court can insist on proof of facts, if the admission is not (SCCH-3) 17 M.V.C.No.361/2020 satisfactory.
In the instant case, since the Court was not satisfied, it wanted the claimants to prove their case independently.
The claimants have miserably failed to prove their case.
"(B) Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 - Accident - Claim petition - Dismissal of - Fraud played on the Courts by the claimants with the connivance of the 1st respondent - Liability of the Insurance Company to pay the compensation if the fraud is proved - Held, Insurance Company not liable to indemnify the owner of the vehicle who has played fraud and not liable to pay any compensation to the claimants who are also party to the fraud - Further Held, It is a clear case of fraud played on the Court by the claimants with the connivance of 1st respondent.
Once the insured plays fraud,
admits liability with the sole object of foisting liability on the Insurance Company,
though in fact he knew that it is not true, liability of the Insurance Company to indemnify such insured ceases.
Dismissal of Claim Petition against the Insurance Company is affirmed".
02. ILR 2009 KAR 2921 in a case of Bajaj Allianz Insurance Company Limited V/s B.C.Kumar and another, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has held that, Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 - Accident claim - Award - Insurance Company Appeal - Plea of Guilt by the driver - Conviction in the criminal case - Can the plea of guilt by the driver become the sole criterion for allowing the claim T.R. Vinayaka vs Veeresh Patil on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56067937/
At the most, the circumstance of the driver pleading guilty may be considered as one of the pieces of evidence to support the case of the claimant.
But, the tribunal should not place implicit reliance only on the circumstance of the driver having pleaded guilty before the Criminal Court and such an approach by the tribunals will be not only an one sided approach but, at the same time, there is every likelihood of the pleading of guilt by a driver before the Criminal Court having been obtained by adopting various methods so as to ensure that the claimant succeeds before the MACT in getting compensation.
The MACTs are constituted not only to allow the claim petitions which are genuine in nature but, at the same time,
the tribunals also will have to keep in view that compensation should not be awarded mechanically in every case and to accept the case of the claimant as if all that the claimant says about the accident and the injuries is a truthful one.
But petitioner has not examined the said eye- witness and even not examined the Investigation (SCCH-3) 21 M.V.C.No.361/2020 Officer to prove the fact that the insured vehicle was actually involved in the accident and no other vehicle was involved in the accident and even no visible damages was found to the insured vehicle as it is alleged that the said offending vehicle has dashed against behind the Motor Cycle of the petitioner, certainly offending vehicle should have damaged and no such damage was found and even petitioner has not produced MLC to proof of involvement of insured vehicle.
Therefore, the petitioner has failed to prove the involvement of the insured vehicle in the accident and rash and negligent riding of the rider of the insured vehicle.
As discussed above, the petitioner has miserably failed to prove the involvement of insured vehicle in the accident and rash and negligent riding by its rider, certainly the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation from the hands of this tribunal.
